title: Etale descent of line modules on an algebraic space
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $F$ an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], and $\{q_i:V_i\to F\}_{i\in I}$ a jointly surjective family of etale maps with each $V_i$ a scheme. Put $R_{ij}=V_i\times_FV_j$, a scheme by representability of the diagonal, with projections $p_i,p_j$. For every $i$ let $M_i$ be an ordinary invertible $\mathcal O_{V_i}$-module [def-sc-invertible-module], and suppose given isomorphisms $\alpha_{ij}:p_j^*M_j\xrightarrow{\sim}p_i^*M_i$ which restrict to the identity on each diagonal and satisfy $\alpha_{ik}=\alpha_{ij}\circ\alpha_{jk}$ after pullback to $V_i\times_FV_j\times_FV_k$. Then there is a line module $M$ on $F$ with identifications $q_i^*M\simeq M_i$ inducing the specified $\alpha_{ij}$. Here restrictions to a scheme are interpreted as ordinary invertible modules via the equivalence between quasi-coherent modules on its Zariski and small etale sites. Moreover, for any two line modules $M,N$ on $F$, restriction is a bijection from $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_F}(M,N)$ to the families of module maps $q_i^*M\to q_i^*N$ agreeing on every $R_{ij}$.

source.place: Tag 04W8 (proposition-fpqc-descent-quasi-coherent), restricted to etale covers; rank-one case of Tag 060X (lemma-finite-locally-free-descends). proof.text: Work on the small site $F_{\mathrm{et}}$ with its structure sheaf as defined in [def-trf-algebraic-space], choosing a small skeleton and a universe containing $I$ and $I\times I$ as in [def-weil-size-convention]. By [lem-trf-scheme-etale-invertible-comparison], set $L_i=A_{V_i}(M_i)$; these are line modules. Its pullback compatibility turns $\alpha_{ij}$ into isomorphisms $a_{ij}:L_j|_{R_{ij}}\to L_i|_{R_{ij}}$ on the small etale site of $R_{ij}$. The same compatibility for composition identifies the ordinary triple-pullback equation with $a_{ik}=a_{ij}a_{jk}$ and identifies diagonal restriction with the identity. No strict identification of distinct iterated module pullbacks is being assumed.

source.place: Tags 03DX, 05VG and 03LC, comparison and pullback compatibility

proof.text: For each test scheme $W\to F$ put $W_i=W\times_F V_i$ and $W_{ij}=W\times_F V_i\times_F V_j$. These are schemes by the representable diagonal; they are etale test objects over the appropriate $V_i$ and $R_{ij}$ by the base-change meaning of etaleness in [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Define set-valued presheaves $H_i(W)=L_i(W_i)$ and $K_{ij}(W)=L_i(W_{ij})$, with restrictions induced by fibre products. They are sheaves: a covering $\{W_b\to W\}$ pulls back to coverings of $W_i$ and $W_{ij}$, and their double intersections are the corresponding pullbacks of $W_b\times_WW_c$. Consequently the sheaf equalizer axiom [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology](1) for $L_i$ is exactly that for $H_i$ or $K_{ij}$. This verification does not require $F$ to be a scheme or a terminal object of $F_{\mathrm{et}}$.

source.place: Tag 04TR (lemma-glue-sheaves), component sheaves in the compatible-tuples construction

proof.text:
There are two natural maps $\prod_i H_i\rightrightarrows\prod_{i,j}K_{ij}$, with coordinates $s_i|_{W_{ij}}$ and $a_{ij}(s_j|_{W_{ij}})$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaf-sets-limits-sectionwise](1) on $F_{\mathrm{et}}$ first to the discrete index categories $I$ and $I\times I$, then to the finite parallel-pair diagram. Its small-index hypothesis holds in the universe fixed in Step 1. The equalizer is a sheaf with the explicit values
$$M(W)=\{(s_i)\in\prod_i L_i(W_i):s_i|_{W_{ij}}=a_{ij}(s_j|_{W_{ij}})\text{ for every }i,j\}.$$
Restrictions act coordinatewise; their compatibility with these equations follows from naturality of $a_{ij}$.

source.place: Tag 04TR (lemma-glue-sheaves), compatible-tuples formula; Tag 00W2 (lemma-limit-sheaf) for its sheaf property

proof.text: Give $M(W)$ coordinatewise addition and inverse, and let $b\in\mathcal O_F(W)$ act on its $i$th coordinate by the restriction of $b$ to $W_i$. Each $a_{ij}$ is linear over $\mathcal O_F(W_{ij})$, so the compatibility equations are closed under these operations and contain zero. All abelian-group and module laws hold coordinatewise because they hold in $L_i(W_i)$. For $W'\to W$ the restriction is semilinear, since restriction in each $L_i$ is semilinear over the induced restriction of functions. Thus the sheaf of sets in Step 3 is a sheaf of $\mathcal O_F$-modules in precisely the sectionwise sense of [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category].

source.place: Tag 04TR, compatible-tuples construction with module operations; Modules on Sites Tag 03CV (definition-sheaf-modules)

proof.text: For an etale $W\to V_a$ let $d_a:W\to W_a$ be its graph over $F$. Define $e_{a,W}:M(W\to F)\to L_a(W)$ by $e_{a,W}((s_i))=d_a^*s_a$. For $y\in L_a(W)$ define $i_{a,W}(y)$ by coordinates $s_i=a_{ia}(y|_{W_i})$, evaluating $a_{ia}$ using the map $W_i\to R_{ia}$ furnished by its $V_i$-projection and $W_i\to W\to V_a$. On $W_{ij}$ the cocycle gives $a_{ij}(s_j|)=a_{ij}a_{ja}(y|)=a_{ia}(y|)=s_i|$, so this is a tuple in $M(W)$. Both formulas are linear. For $h:W'\to W$ over $V_a$, the graph equation $h_a d'_a=d_a h$ proves restriction compatibility of $e_a$; naturality of $a_{ia}$ proves it coordinatewise for $i_a$. Hence these formulas define module-sheaf maps on $(V_a)_{\mathrm{et}}$.

source.place: Tag 04TR, explicit graph evaluation and inverse for the local gluing isomorphisms

proof.text: The composite $e_ai_a$ is identity because $a_{aa}$ restricts to identity along the diagonal of $V_a$. For a compatible tuple $s$ and any $i$, pull its $(i,a)$ equation back along $W_i\to W_{ia}$ whose $a$-coordinate is the given $W\to V_a$. This yields $s_i=a_{ia}((d_a^*s_a)|_{W_i})$, so $i_ae_a$ is identity too. Thus $e_a:q_a^*M\simeq L_a$. For a test scheme $W\to R_{ab}$, pull the $(a,b)$ tuple equation back along the graph $W\to W_{ab}$ of both structural maps: it becomes $e_a=a_{ab}e_b$. This proves that the local identifications induce exactly the prescribed transition isomorphisms, including self-overlaps; $a_{aa}$ was used as identity only on its diagonal.

source.place: Tag 04TR, explicit verification of the inverse and of transition compatibility

proof.text: Choose Zariski trivializing covers of each $M_a$, as permitted by [def-sc-invertible-module]. By [lem-trf-scheme-etale-invertible-comparison], their associated etale modules are trivial with structure-module identification $A(\mathcal O)\simeq\mathcal O$. For any test object $W\to F$, the schemes $W_a$ cover $W$; further pullback of the trivializing covers covers each $W_a$. The composition-of-coverings axiom [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology](1) gives a covering of $W$ on which $M$ is the structure module, using $e_a$ from Step 6. Thus $M$ is a line module as defined in [def-trf-algebraic-space]. The same comparison equivalence interprets $e_a$ as $q_a^*M\simeq M_a$ in ordinary invertible modules, and its faithfulness makes the transition identity of Step 6 the original $\alpha_{ab}$.

source.place: Tag 060X (lemma-finite-locally-free-descends), etale-local rank-one specialization; here verified directly with local frames

proof.text: Finally let $M,N$ be any line modules on $F$, and let compatible ordinary module maps on the $V_i$ be given. Full faithfulness and pullback compatibility of [lem-trf-scheme-etale-invertible-comparison] turn them into maps $g_i:M|_{V_i}\to N|_{V_i}$ agreeing on every overlap. For $s\in M(W)$ put $t_i=g_i(s|_{W_i})\in N(W_i)$. Agreement and naturality give $t_i|_{W_{ij}}=t_j|_{W_{ij}}$. The sheaf axiom [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology](1) yields a unique $t\in N(W)$ restricting to all $t_i$; set $g_W(s)=t$. For $W'\to W$, both restrictions of this formula have the same values on all $W'_i$, so separatedness makes $g$ natural. Additivity and $\mathcal O_F(W)$-linearity follow by the same uniqueness, applied to $s+s'$ and $bs$. For $W\to V_i$, restrict the defining equality on $W_i$ along its graph $W\to W_i$; this gives $g_W(s)=g_i(s)$. A second global map with the same restrictions agrees on every $W_i$ and hence on $W$ by separatedness. This proves surjectivity and injectivity of the asserted restriction map.

lean.note: Retains ordinary Scheme.Modules.IsInvertible local modules and the specified ordinary tensor-pullback overlap isomorphisms. OrdinaryEtaleIdentification is the sectionwise linear/natural form of the localized-site isomorphism with the ordinary associated etale module. InvertibleAtlasDescentDatum bundles exactly the overlap isomorphisms, diagonal identity and triple cocycle; its tests range over all schemes over the base. The final conjunct is full faithfulness, stated as unique gluing of compatible localized module maps. All transport helpers have explicit data from the existing canonical tensor-pullback units and composition isomorphisms; no inverse equivalence or unrelated global extensions are assumed.
